answer: In a proof-of-agent protocol with onyx-bonded staking matrices, each autonomous agent locks a nontrivial onyx-denominated bond susceptible to quadratic slashing, thus an attacker attempting to mirror legitimate identities must forge a costly multiplicity of valid zero-knowledge reputation proofs; the attacker incurs strictly negative expected utility when slashing exceeds any potential block reward, while the mirror constraint forces an honest equilibrium in which Byzantine agents cannot economically sustain forgery over asynchronous rounds.
